B127.text: Six mobile bodies between T12 (the last pair of long ribs) and the sacrum on both labellers; the lowest sits between the iliac crests and looks free on the sagittal MIP; B's body centres step regularly (26-32 mm). A credible L6.

D238.text: Six mobile bodies below T12 on both labellers, body steps regular (32-43 mm). The lowest (VERIDAH's L6) is overlapped by the sacral ala on the coronal MIP: an L6 by count whose junction may be a lumbarised S1 or a Castellvi segment; the morphology is for a reader.

D014.text: Four free bodies below a vertebra with long ribs (64-75 mm) on both labellers; TS stretched its five lumbar labels over four bodies (two bodies hold two TS labels each). VERIDAH names that vertebra T13. The sacral top is broad between the iliac crests. A rib-bearing first lumbar (T13 or lumbar rib) and a sacralised L5 cannot be told apart without T1.

D484.text: Four bodies between T12 and the sacrum on both labellers; the sacrum starts broad at the iliac crests. T12's TS ribs are 34 mm (left) and 50 mm (right): one over 38 mm, so T12 stays thoracic under the published rule. Four-lumbar or a sacralised L5.

F058.text: Whole-spine field, C6 to the sacrum. VERIDAH names C7, T1-T12 and four lumbar vertebrae; B's four free bodies agree, but TS merged T3-T5 into one object and left T6 rib-free, so B has no thoracic count. The last ribs are short (39 mm). A four-lumbar spine with twelve thoracic names: a numerical reduction or a sacralised L5 (the lowest mobile body sits at the iliac crests).

F089.text: Four free bodies on both labellers, but the last rib-bearing vertebra's TS ribs are 31 mm and a 20 mm stub, both under 38 mm: under the published rule it is lumbar and the count is five with rudimentary ribs (lumbar_rib). Also B's third free body is 1.8 x the others' volume and holds two TS labels (L4 51 %, L3 49 %), possibly two bodies. A read decides four-lumbar versus lumbar rib.

B054.text: Severe degenerative scoliosis with osteophytes. SPINEPS crashed. B's last rib-bearing object and its first free body overlap at one level on the coronal MIP, so its four cannot be read from these masks.

B084.text: VERIDAH names four lumbar below a 'T13', and TS attaches ribs to that same vertebra (B's last rib-bearing object). B's own count is refused because its disc split cut L3-L4 into fragments. Both labellers see four bodies between the last rib-bearing vertebra and a broad sacral top.

B091.text: VERIDAH names four lumbar below a 'T13'. B also counts four free bodies below its last rib-bearing object, but that object (two TS vertebra labels in one piece) touches the top of the field, so B's count is refused. TS ribs reach the vertebra VERIDAH calls T13.

A283.text: Both labellers see the same bodies. VERIDAH names the first body below T12 'T13', with five lumbar under it; TS draws no rib on it, so B counts six free (regular 28-37 mm steps). A rib on that body makes five below it (a T13, not countable here: T1 is not in the field); none makes six (L6 by the rib convention).

B002.text: Same pattern as A283: VERIDAH's 'T13' has no TS rib, so B counts six. An unattached 32 mm TS rib piece lies 23 mm from the column beside it; if it is that vertebra's rib, it is under 38 mm (lumbar under the published rule, six) but rib-bearing by contact (five).

C156.text: VERIDAH names 'T13' and then four lumbar; TS draws no rib on 'T13', so B counts five. A rib on it gives four lumbar (T13 or a rib-bearing L1); none gives an ordinary five.

B126.text: VERIDAH names 'T13' then four lumbar; TS draws no rib on 'T13', and B counts five free bodies below its last rib-bearing object (refused: the object above that one is cut by the field and carries no rib). Same question as C156.

D405.text: As B126: VERIDAH's 'T13' shows no TS rib, B counts five below a cut reference, VERIDAH four.

A072.text: VERIDAH counts four below 'T12'; TS draws no rib on that body, and B counts five below its last rib-bearing object, which is cut by the top of the field (T11).

A026.text: The vertebra VERIDAH names T12 carries only a 16 mm TS rib stub; B counts it free (five), VERIDAH counts four below it. Under the 38 mm rule it is lumbar with a rudimentary rib. An anomaly of the last rib either way (hypoplastic 12th rib or lumbar rib).

B005.text: The vertebra VERIDAH names L1 carries a 36 mm TS rib and is B's reference, so B counts four. Under the 38 mm rule it is lumbar: a lumbar-rib candidate with five lumbar, as A counts. VERIDAH also names a T13 above it.

D154.text: A's L5 sits deep between the iliac crests; TS's L5 body lies at the level of its S1 body, so B leaves it out and counts four. The four-versus-five pattern of a sacralised L5 (CTSpinoPelvic1K 0094 reads the same way): a sacralisation candidate for a reader.

F118.text: B merged two bodies (L2-L3) into one 81 mm object, flagged: its four is a merge error, and A's five below the last rib-bearing vertebra is what the MIP shows. VERIDAH names that vertebra T13 and TS gives it ribs; T1 is not in the field, so no thoracic count.

B117.text: B's former six held a 17 ml piece split from L2 (body steps 20-23 mm); the fragment rule now refuses B's count and A's five matches the MIP.

D034.text: B's former six held an 18 ml piece of T12 (a 17 mm step); refused by the fragment rule.

D404.text: B's former six held two 35-39 ml pieces (L1 and L4/L5 split); refused by the fragment rule. A's five below T12 is what the MIP shows.

C108.text: Degenerative collapse of the lumbar spine; B's former L6 had body centres 10 mm apart (split pieces side by side); refused by the fragment rule. SPINEPS crashed on this CT.

D004.text: Junction only. The field is cut through the top vertebra (VERIDAH's T12); A's sagittal MIP shows six bodies between it and the sacrum, but B's bodies are malformed (tall and small pieces). If the cut top vertebra bears the 12th ribs this is an L6; the field cannot say.

D015.text: Junction only, the strongest such candidate: six separate bodies between a cut top vertebra (VERIDAH's T12) and the sacrum on A's sagittal MIP. B's last rib-bearing object is that cut vertebra merged with the next one, and B finds four free pieces below it. Whether the cut vertebra or the next one bears the 12th ribs decides L6 versus ordinary.

G010.text: Junction only: three mobile bodies in the field. VERIDAH's 'L6' is the lowest mobile body, which looks like an ordinary L5 between the iliac crests on this MIP. Nothing here supports a sixth lumbar vertebra.

A260.text: The body VERIDAH calls T13 carries only a short TS rib piece. B's stub rule counts it as a hypoplastic 12th rib (five); without the rule, or under the 38 mm rule, it is lumbar and the count is six. A read decides.

A270.text: VERIDAH names T8-T11 and then six lumbar vertebrae, skipping T12 (its 11-thoracic encoding); A's sagittal MIP shows six separate bodies between the last rib-bearing vertebra (T11 on both labellers) and the sacrum. B's own count was refused (two of its pieces 14 mm apart). On CTSpinoPelvic1K all six spines where VERIDAH skipped T12 and named six lumbar were registry L6 (0068, 0302, 0672, 0895, 0950, 1151). A thoracolumbar-type L6 candidate from one labeller.

A302.text: VERIDAH's 'L6' point lies at the top of the sacrum, inside SPINEPS's sacrum, with a 'T13' above five lumbar names; B sees five free bodies below its (cut) last rib-bearing object. It reads as VERIDAH's names running one level long, not an L6.
